Hi all — attaching a draft of the things Alice asked for and a short technical note on validation we ran. High-level points for the appendix: 

- Isolation model (summary): Each customer deployment on Redwood Private runs in a logically isolated tenant VPC (or VNet). The control plane is deployed in a separate management VPC accessible only over mTLS-authenticated control channels and private peering; no control-plane API endpoints are publicly routable.

- Data-plane tenancy: GPU hosts run tenant workloads inside container sandboxes with strict namespace/mount isolation. Network isolation is enforced with per-tenant virtual routing instances and distributed ACLs. Tenant traffic egress traverses an egress gateway owned per-tenant (SNAT) or per-customer NAT with optional VPC egress gateway.

- Egress controls and monitoring: Egress is deny-by-default. Customers may request outbound whitelist entries via PR that results in a per-tenant rule in the edge NAT cluster. All rule changes are recorded in the change log and emit events to our audit pipeline (CloudTrail-equivalent). We collect host-level flow logs and VPC flow logs; a daily job samples and archives flows used for the evidence matrix.

- Controls mapping (short):
  • Network isolation: VRF/route table per tenant + ACLs (evidence: tenant-egress-matrix.xlsx — sheet 'net-isolation')
  • Control plane separation: Private control-plane VPC peering + firewall policy (evidence: network-diagrams-v2.pdf)
  • Egress enforcement: Egress gateway (SNAT) + eBPF-based filtering at the edge (evidence: edge-snat-diagram.png, egress-test-run-20261215.csv)
  • Auditability: CloudTrail stream + immutable S3 bucket with retention policy + hashed manifests (evidence: cloudtrail-pointer.txt - redacted)

Planned deliverables attached: redacted network diagram (network-diagrams-v2.pdf), tenant egress matrix (tenant-egress-matrix.xlsx), and an operational diagram for the edge NAT/SNAT cluster (edge-snat-diagram.png). For the SIG bundle we will provide redacted config snippets and one representative packet capture demonstrating SNAT translation for outbound traffic.

Notes on redaction: we will remove internal IP ranges and replace with labeled ranges (TENANT_A_IP_RANGE) and strip hostnames. We will keep control-plane CIDR labeling intact but not publish internal host identifiers.

ETA: I can deliver the drafts by EOD 2026-12-21. Laura — can you confirm the set of logs we are comfortable sharing (we should avoid PII and customer-specific flow samples)?

–Karthik
